review_scope: Independent primary-literature identity, exact gene membership, scoring definition, prior cohort use and claim-boundary check for 001C. No expression analyses; no independent validation expression downloaded.

articles.title: Metabolism and response to stress gene signatures reveal ulcerative colitis heterogeneity and identify patients with increased response to therapy
articles.published: 2025-06-09 publisher online date; EuropePMC firstPublicationDate 2025-06-01 is month-level metadata
articles.original_definition: 11 separate Reactome components, derived from MSigDB v7.4 signature scores. GSVA/GSEA used; 5 components correlate negatively with RHI, 6 positively. Unsupervised Euclidean complete-linkage clustering of baseline multicomponent profiles; not one weighted small-gene score.
articles.original_score_reproducibility: Exact 11 named components and published membership retained. Exact numerical GSVA/clustering recreation not established: method options not fully specified, original andecaliximab source data supplied by Gilead, no complete source-model object in retrieved materials. Our gene means are explicitly comparator proxies.
articles.public_cohort_use: Baseline anti-TNF datasets combined by ComBat for therapy-response subgroup analysis; GSE73661 infliximab portion was used, not a claim that all vedolizumab trajectories were analyzed.
articles.private_original_data: Andecaliximab trial GS-US-326-1100 mucosal RNAseq, baseline and week 8, provided by Gilead; public signature files do not make this source dataset anonymously accessible.
articles.known_conclusion: Metabolic/stress dimensions beyond a single inflammation score stratify UC and associate with treatment response; simple metabolic recovery or low-inflammatory/high-nondisease baseline profiles are not new by themselves.
articles.membership_issues: Literal PDF columns misplace FOS, GSTK1, LONP2, STAT2, JAK3 and TBK1 to preceding columns. Six explicitly documented layout-reassignment hypotheses yield 10/11 sets identical to MSigDB 7.4. SARS: literal column 35, layout-aligned 37, original-version GMT 81; cannot silently declare these equivalent.
usable_variants: program_gene_membership_layout_sensitivity.tsv: MARS_TableS1_layout_inference_* proposed column alignment; not author-confirmed

articles.title: Endoscopic healing in pediatric IBD perpetuates a persistent signature defined by Th17 cells with molecular and microbial drivers of disease
articles.direction: Persistently upregulated tissue genes; higher original IBrD values mean greater residual molecular disease.
articles.original_definition: 81 network-selected persistent genes -> PCA -> minimum PCs explaining 80% variance -> slingshot principal curve -> normalized pseudotime on [0,1]. New samples require original feature centers/scales, PCA rotations and fitted curve; author code projects to the original trajectory.
articles.original_score_reproducibility: Not currently reproducible as original fitted score: authors' public README says contact lead authors for SCE and prcomp objects. Code also has argument/global-object inconsistencies (sce_obj/pca_obj versus sce/pca); no execution was attempted. A simple mean/GSVA is not the original IBrD score.
articles.author_repository_access: Public guest FTP code obtained using credentials explicitly published on repository landing page; main code, README, license and sessionInfo saved. No Data directory files downloaded.
articles.cohort_use: External validation of molecular residual disease versus non-IBD and Mayo endoscopic groups; 26 of 81 genes identified on that external technical platform in the original report.
articles.other_two_GSEs: No use of GSE92415 or GSE23597 identified in retrieved full text or signature supplement.
articles.known_conclusion: Endoscopic healing does not imply complete molecular normalization; persistent epithelial/immune stress and Th17-related disease features already established. Residual disease after apparent healing is not a novel overarching concept.
articles.usable_proxy: IBrD_unweighted_gene_mean_proxy; report actual assay coverage; use association/overlap comparison only, not original IBrD reproduction or calibrated 0-1 score.

articles.title: JAK/STAT signaling promotes the emergence of unique cell states in ulcerative colitis
articles.IA13_direction: Upregulated in inflammation-associated colonocytes and goblet cells relative to their respective lineages. Authors functionally relate these states to IL22/JAKSTAT and increased regenerative properties in organoids.
articles.author_marker_sets: All reported Table S2 markers for exact Celltype Colonocytes or CT Colonocytes, 20 each. No expression-derived rescreening or extra P/logFC cutoffs. Complete as reported in table, not claimed to be entire source list of every significant gene.
articles.HMGCS2_scope: Not among the 20 reported markers per cell type in this supplement; absence does not establish novelty or no relationship to mature colonocytes.
articles.known_conclusion: Inflammation-associated epithelial states can have increased regenerative capacity while lineage-differentiation markers decline. Thus inflammation/stress, regeneration and terminal maturation must not be treated as the same axis.
articles.source_defined_not_new: IA13 is author-published. The full 20-marker lineage sets are author-reported. The optional four-marker CA1/CA2/KRT20/CEACAM1 proxy is assembled here from individual source markers and is not an author score; KRT20/CEACAM1 are shared crypt-top differentiation markers rather than exclusively colonocyte abundance.

already_known: Five of six candidate genes already annotate differentiated colonocyte states in a primary UC single-cell study.
MARS already linked non-inflammatory metabolism/stress programs to baseline UC treatment-response heterogeneity, using all three intended bulk cohorts.
IBrD already established persistent molecular disease after endoscopic healing and validated this in GSE73661.
Inflammation-associated/regenerative cell programs and terminal differentiation are biologically distinct in primary UC experiments.
not_sufficient_for_novelty: No gene overlap with MARS/IBrD does not prove independent biological information.
Renaming existing lineage markers as a new recovery signature is not a genuine increment.
GSE73661 is independent of our discovery patients, but not a never-used novelty cohort; same cohort reuse needs a different relation/question.
A mean expression proxy cannot be compared as if it reproduced the authors' original calibrated score.
testable_increment: A defined patient-level longitudinal relationship between inflammatory decline and mature-colonocyte restoration after therapy, if it remains distinct from published lineage, IA13 and MARS component proxies and survives held-out validation.
Whether the six-gene candidate is simply a compressed mature-colonocyte marker average can be tested directly against the unchanged author-reported 20-marker sets.
Biopsy composition versus cell-intrinsic expression should be distinguished in later single-cell work; bulk association alone cannot settle this.
claim_boundary.novelty_search_limit: This is a bounded prior-definition/citation audit, not exhaustive proof that the exact longitudinal relationship has never been published. Do not freeze a novel signature on this audit alone.

outstanding_scoring_limits: IBrD original fitted PCA/SCE/curve objects not supplied publicly; authors request needed for authentic projection.
MARS exact score options and SARS membership discrepancy unresolved; proxies and named membership sensitivities are acceptable if labeled.
No validation expression used or new statistical result created in this review.

definition_verification.scope: Membership transcription and direct source comparison only; no expression statistics or original scoring reproduction
